# Part 1: Data verification & tidy data

## 1.1 Data import

Process
- Keep only data we will use - then tidy/wrangle data incl. for filtering and verification
- kept : `Sample` for eventual verification and variables for grouping for figures: 
    - `ST`/`Serotype` renamed and coerced to character here so nothing downstream touches the raw `mlst_scheme_list/sequence_type` / `SeroTypeFinder/SeroType` names.
    - `Production` type (driftsformnavn), `Species` host (artnavn), `Year` and `Case` (sak) to be able to know the number of cases registred. 
    - I only used the excel sheet `APEC_driftsformsjekk_120226 (2)` of the excel file: `Results_130226_SSM.xlsx`
- I had to only keep those columns then for adding to zenodo (remove extra to avoid producent info.)

```{r load data}
isolates_raw <- read_excel(
  here::here(params$results_xlsx),
  sheet = params$isolate_sheet
) %>%
  # keeping only relevant columns
  select(
    Sample, Year, 
    Case = sak,
    ST = `mlst_scheme_list/sequence_type`,
    Serotype = `SeroTypeFinder/SeroType`,
    Production = driftsformnavn,
    Species = artnavn
  ) %>%
  mutate(ST = as.character(ST), Year = as.integer(Year))
```

## 1.2 Data verification

### 1.2.1 Completeness check:

One row per isolate, and the fields every downstream figure depends on
(year, ST, serotype, production type) must be complete.

```{r qc checks}
qc <- list(
  n_rows = nrow(isolates_raw),
  n_distinct_sample = n_distinct(isolates_raw$Sample),
  n_missing_year = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Year)),
  n_missing_case = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Case)),
  n_missing_ST = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$ST)),
  n_missing_serotype = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Serotype)),
  n_missing_production = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Production)),
  n_missing_species = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Species))
  )

qc

stopifnot(
  "one row per isolate expected" = qc$n_rows == qc$n_distinct_sample,
  "Year must be complete" = qc$n_missing_year == 0,
  "ST must be complete" = qc$n_missing_ST == 0,
  "Serotype must be complete" = qc$n_missing_serotype == 0,
  "Production must be complete" = qc$n_missing_production == 0
)
```

::: {.callout-note title="data completeness"}
884 rows  - and all distinct samples - no missing data
:::

### 1.2.2 Category spelling / homogeneity check

`check_spelling_homogeneity()` flags pairs of values in a column that are
identical after trimming/casefolding ("case_or_whitespace" - safe to
auto-fix) or within a small edit distance ("possible_typo" - needs a human
read).

Tolerance differs by column: `Production`/`Species` are free text, so a
1-2 character difference is almost always a typo (`max_dist = 2`); `ST`/
`Serotype` are nomenclature codes where a 1-character difference is usually a
genuinely different code (`O1:H4` vs. `O1:H7`), so only exact
case/whitespace collisions are flagged (`max_dist = 0`).
Moreover those should be automatically assigned so it should not be any errors


```{r spelling checks}
spelling_flags <- bind_rows(
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Production, max_dist = 2) %>% mutate(column = "Production"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Species, max_dist = 2) %>% mutate(column = "Species"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$ST, max_dist = 0) %>% mutate(column = "ST"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Serotype, max_dist = 0) %>% mutate(column = "Serotype")
) %>%
  relocate(column)

spelling_flags

write_csv(spelling_flags, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "spelling_flags.csv"))
```

- problems reading norwegian special characters - got corrupted sometimes
> This is why data usually does not use special characters - this simplifies the work. 

- fixed below: `Production` has a known mojibake artifact
("Foreldredyr, kjøttproduksjon" vs. corrupted "Foreldredyr,
kj�ttproduksjon", 2 rows)
- `Species` has one genuine case duplicate
("Rowan ranger" vs. "Rowan Ranger" 
- the other near-neighbours are real, distinct breed names and are correctly not flagged)
- `ST`/`Serotype` have nothing flagged. (expected given code ! - Trivial)

```{r fix flagged values}
isolates_fixed <- isolates_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Production = if_else(
      Production == "Foreldredyr, kj�ttproduksjon",
      "Foreldredyr, kjøttproduksjon",
      Production),
    Species = if_else(
      Species == "Rowan Ranger",
      "Rowan ranger",
      Species)
    ) 
```

Manual verification
```{r verifying spelling, eval=FALSE}
my_summary_fun(isolates_fixed, Sample) %>%
  write_csv(file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "manual_check.csv"))
```


::: {.callout-important title="Asked questions / decisions (Solveig)"}
- ONT and HNT kept as is - same for the multiple serotypes with /- see bellow for Species grouping - also decided (Solveig)

**Categories species grouping/renaming:**
- "Hubbard JA 787" as "Hubbard"
- "Ross" as "Ross 308"
:::

## 1.4 Cleaning: production type (broiler / parent flock)
And transforming Norwegian to English 
```{r clean driftsform}
isolates <- isolates_fixed %>%
  mutate(
    production_type = case_when(
      str_starts(Production, "Foreldredyr") ~ "Parent",
      Production == "Kjøttproduksjon" ~ "Broiler",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    production_type = factor(production_type, levels = c("Broiler", "Parent")),
    Year = as.integer(Year)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Species = case_when(
        Species == "Høns" ~ "Chicken",
        Species == "Hubbard" ~ "Hubbard",
        Species == "Hubbard JA 787" ~ "Hubbard",
        Species == "Ross" ~ "Ross 308",
        Species == "Ross 308" ~ "Ross 308",
        Species == "Ross rowan" ~ "Ross rowan",
        Species == "Rowan 308" ~ "Rowan 308",
        Species == "Rowan Ranger" ~ "Rowan ranger",
        Species == "Rustic gold" ~ "Rustic gold",
        Species == "Sasso" ~ "Sasso",
        TRUE ~ Species
      ),
      Species = factor(Species, levels = c(
        "Chicken",  "Ross 308", "Hubbard", "Ross rowan", "Rowan 308", "Rowan ranger", "Rustic gold", "Sasso")
      )
    ) %>%
    select(-Production)

stopifnot("production_type must be complete after recoding" = sum(is.na(isolates$production_type)) == 0)
stopifnot("Species must be complete after recoding" = sum(is.na(isolates$Species)) == 0)
count(isolates, production_type)
count(isolates, Species)

```

## 1.5 New variable: `variant` (ST-Serotype combination)

Requested format: `ST23-O78:H4`.

```{r variant column}
isolates <- isolates %>%
  mutate(
    ST = paste0("ST", ST),
    variant = paste0(ST, "-", Serotype)
    )

n_distinct(isolates$variant)  # 134 distinct ST-Serotype combinations observed
head(count(isolates, variant, sort = TRUE), 5)
```

## 1.6 ST, Serotype, variant contingency tables evaluation - top 5 / top 10

> preparation for data visualisation: 

Same question, two groupings: 
- keep the top N *variants*, how many distinct ST/Serotype does that represent
- keep the top N *ST*s instead, how many
distinct Serotype/variant. 

Same `top_n_contingency()` pattern for both, just a different `group_col` /
`other_cols` - shared helpers (`kept_vs_other()`, `total_distinct_values()`,
`add_proportions()`, all in `code/R/`)

```{r contingency helpers}
# how many distinct values of ST/Serotype/variant exist overall, to turn

# n_distinct_values (below) into a percentage of "how much of the diversity"
total_distinct <- total_distinct_values(isolates, c("ST", "Serotype", "variant"))
total_distinct
```


### Grouped by variant

> to see at which level we need to group for the figures 

```{r top n variant contingency}
variant_contingency_top5 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "variant", top_n = 5, other_cols = c("ST", "Serotype"))


variant_contingency_top10 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "variant", top_n = 10, other_cols = c("ST", "Serotype"))

variant_threshold_summary <- bind_rows(
  kept_vs_other(variant_contingency_top5, 5),
  kept_vs_other(variant_contingency_top10, 10)
) %>%
  add_proportions(total_distinct, nrow(isolates))

write_tsv(variant_threshold_summary, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "variant_grouping_threshold_summary.tsv"))

variant_threshold_summary
```

- keeping the top 5 variants covers 417/884 isolates (47.2%) but
names only 5/88 STs (5.7%) and 5/115 serotypes (4.3%) - the "other" bucket is the minority of isolates (467, 52.8%) yet holds nearly all of the diversity (97.7% of STs, 99.1% of serotypes). 

- Top 10 covers more isolates (550/884,
62.2%) at a similar diversity trade-off - 8 STs (9.1%) and 10 serotypes (8.7%) named, 94.3%/95.7% still in "other". Neither threshold captures much ST/Serotype diversity - that's inherent to a "top N" cut on data this skewed (one variant, ST23-O78:H4, is 244/884 isolates - 27.6% - on its own), not a flaw in the threshold choice.

### Grouped by ST

```{r top n ST contingency}
ST_contingency_top5 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "ST", top_n = 5, other_cols = c("Serotype", "variant"))

ST_contingency_top10 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "ST", top_n = 10, other_cols = c("Serotype", "variant"))

ST_threshold_summary <- bind_rows(
  kept_vs_other(ST_contingency_top5, 5),
  kept_vs_other(ST_contingency_top10, 10)
) %>%
  add_proportions(total_distinct, nrow(isolates))

write_tsv(ST_threshold_summary, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "ST_grouping_threshold_summary.tsv"))

ST_threshold_summary
```

Grouping by ST instead captures more diversity per isolate,
because one ST can carry several different serotypes. 
- Top 5 STs cover 505/884 isolates (57.1%) and represent 18/115 serotypes (15.7%) and 19/134 variants (14.2%) - roughly 3-4x the serotype/variant coverage of the top-5 *variant* grouping, for a similar isolate share. "Other" (379 isolates,
42.9%) still holds most of the diversity (103 serotypes, 89.6%; 115 variants, 85.8%). 

- Top 10 STs: 645/884 isolates (73.0%), 23 serotypes (20.0%),
25 variants (18.7%) named; 239 other isolates (27.0%) still cover 98 serotypes (85.2%) and 109 variants (81.3%).

## Preparing for figures 

### 1. Scatter pie chart- top 10 variants choosen.

Top 10 ST-Serotype variants by isolate count, "Other" grouping everything else.

```{r grouped columns top10}
top10_variants_fig7_prep <-
  isolates %>%
  mutate(variant_top10 = top_n_other(variant, 10, other_label = "Other"))
```

```{r getting contingency table for top10 variants fig 7}
top10_variants_fig7 <-
  top10_variants_fig7_prep %>%
  select(Year, variant_top10, production_type) %>%
  group_by(Year, variant_top10, production_type) %>%
  tally()

top10_variants_fig7
write_tsv(top10_variants_fig7, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "data_pie_fig_top10_variant_year_production_tally.tsv"))
```

```{r figure7 top10 pie data}
# x order: top 10 by isolate count (desc), "Other" always last
variant_top10_totals <-
  top10_variants_fig7 %>%
  group_by(variant_top10) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total))

variant_top10_levels <- c(setdiff(variant_top10_totals$variant_top10, "Other"), "Other")
x_spacing <- 1.7  # widens the plot; coord_equal() keeps pies round regardless

fig7_top10_pie_data <-
  top10_variants_fig7 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = production_type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    variant_top10 = factor(variant_top10, levels = variant_top10_levels),
    x = as.numeric(variant_top10) * x_spacing,  # column position, spaced out
    y = Year,
    total = Broiler + `Parent`
  )

fig7_top10_pie_data
```

Pie size uses 4 fixed categories (1-10, 10-50, 50-100, 100-200 isolates)
instead of a continuous scale, so sizes are easy to compare at a glance.
Each category gets one area-corrected radius (sqrt, not linear - a linear
radius would make circle area, which is what a reader actually perceives,
grow with the square of the count and exaggerate differences).

```{r figure7 top10 pie data radius}
max_total_top10 <- max(fig7_top10_pie_data$total)

bin_breaks <- c(1, 10, 50, 100, 200)
bin_labels <- c("1-10", "10-50", "50-100", "100-200")
stopifnot("some isolate counts exceed the largest defined bin (200) - extend bin_breaks" = max_total_top10 <= 200)

# radius per category, from its upper edge, normalized against 200 (category max)
bin_upper <- c(10, 50, 100, 200)
bin_radius <- 0.42 * sqrt(bin_upper / max(bin_upper))
names(bin_radius) <- bin_labels

fig7_top10_pie_data <-
  fig7_top10_pie_data %>%
  mutate(
    total_bin = cut(total, breaks = bin_breaks, labels = bin_labels, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE),
    r = bin_radius[as.character(total_bin)]
  )

fig7_top10_pie_data
write_tsv(
  fig7_top10_pie_data %>% select(Year, variant_top10, Broiler, Parent, total, total_bin),
  file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "fig7_top10_pie_data_binned.tsv")
)
```

r = 0.42 * sqrt(bin_upper / 200) - sqrt keeps circle *area* (not radius)
proportional to isolate count; 0.42 is chosen so the biggest category's
circle fits one grid cell without touching its neighbours.

```{r figure7 top10 pie}
fig7_top10_width_cm <- 55
fig7_top10_height_cm <- 18

base_plot_top10 <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_scatterpie(
    data = fig7_top10_pie_data,
    aes(x = x, y = y, r = r),
    cols = c("Broiler", "Parent"),
    color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(variant_top10_levels) * x_spacing, labels = variant_top10_levels, expand = expansion(add = 0.7)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(fig7_top10_pie_data$Year)), expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2], name = "Production type") +
  labs(x = "Variant", y = "Year") +
  theme_apec_piematrix()

# Legend-size calibration (makes legend same size as plot pies - because legend is added manually)
mm_per_unit_top10 <- panel_mm_per_data_unit(base_plot_top10, fig7_top10_width_cm, fig7_top10_height_cm)  # how many mm is 1 data-unit, once actually rendered at this width/height

bin_radius_mm <- 2 * bin_radius * mm_per_unit_top10  # radius (data-units) -> diameter (mm): x2 for diameter, x mm_per_unit_top10 to convert units

names(bin_radius_mm) <- bin_labels  # re-attach the "1-10"/"10-50"/... names (arithmetic above can drop them) - scale_size_manual() below matches legend entries to sizes BY these names

fig7_top10 <- base_plot_top10 +
  geom_point(data = fig7_top10_pie_data, aes(x = x, y = y, size = total_bin), alpha = 0) +
  scale_size_manual(
    name = "Number of isolates", values = bin_radius_mm, drop = FALSE,
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, shape = 21, color = "grey40", fill = "grey80"))
  )

fig7_top10
save_apec_plot(fig7_top10, "fig7_top10_variant_piematrix_by_year.png", dir = params$figures_dir, width = fig7_top10_width_cm, height = fig7_top10_height_cm)
```



### Sampling distribution: isolates per year by production type

Sampling overview: total isolates collected per year, split by production type.

```{r getting data for fig9 sampling design}
fig9_sampling_design_data <-
  isolates %>%
  group_by(Year, production_type) %>%
  tally()

fig9_sampling_design_data
write_tsv(fig9_sampling_design_data, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "fig9_sampling_design_year_production_tally.tsv"))
```

```{r figure9 sampling design bar}
fig9_sampling_design <-
  ggplot(fig9_sampling_design_data, aes(x = factor(Year), y = n, fill = production_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +  # stacked by default (one fill per Year bar)
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2], name = "Production type") +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Number of isolates") +
  theme_apec()

fig9_sampling_design
save_apec_plot(fig9_sampling_design, "fig9_sampling_design_year_production_bar.png", dir = params$figures_dir, width = 18, height = 12)
```
